newsitem.title: USA: Dole aide accused of marijuana use while student.
newsitem.headline: Dole aide accused of marijuana use while student.

text.p: Bob Dole, who has accused the Clinton administration of being soft on drugs, was hit by allegations on Saturday that his own campaign's communications director smoked marijuana regularly while in college.

The Republican presidential candidate, in an interview with the Hartford Courant newspaper, said he did not think the allegations against campaign director John Buckley undercut his campaign against drug use, saying, "I don't think it has any relevance at all."

Dole, in his interview with reporter Jon Lender, to be published on Sunday, the day that the Republican meets President Bill Clinton in a make-or-break debate in Hartford, Connecticut, also said he had not seen details of the allegations.
"I think McCurry had a problem with that, didn't he?" Dole said, referring to Clinton's press secretary, Mike McCurry, who has previously admitted using marijuana.

Dole's press spokesman, Nelson Warfield, said Dole had not yet had a chance to speak to Buckley and Buckley remained the campaign's communications director and would accompany Dole to Hartford on Sunday.
Warfield added, "I'm sure if John made a mistake in college, he regrets it today."

Buckley, who in a statement on Saturday did not deny trying marijuana, has been a key player in shaping Dole policies, including the candidate's attack on drug use. A Dole campaign TV spot targets Clinton's admission in an MTV interview that he tried marijuana once and wished he had inhaled.
"Bill Clinton doesn't get it," the announcer said. "But we do." A final graphic reads, "Clinton's liberal drug policy has failed."

In recent campaign appearances, Dole has accused Clinton of being soft on drugs, saying, "Thanks to the liberal, wink-and-a-nod policies of this administration, drug use among teenagers has not just started up again but it's skyrocketing."

Buckley's statement said, "Whether I or any member of the Dole or Clinton staff used marijuana 20 years ago when in college is not a relevant issue and I'm not going to respond to further questions on the subject."

The allegations against Buckley, a nephew of conservative columnist William Buckley, were first aired in a Boston weekly newspaper last month and then late on Friday by ABC's affiliate TV station in Washington.

A former college roommate, Ed Benfey, told Reuters that Buckley was a regular user of marijuana while at Hampshire College in western Massachusetts more than 20 years ago. He described the liberal school as a place where "pot-smoking was the rule, not the exception."
"Yes, he smoked pot. So what? A lot of people smoked pot. It was socially acceptable in that place and time to smoke pot," Benfey said in a telephone interview from his Long Island, New York, home.
"It was the rule to smoke pot, not the exception. No one ever thought twice about it. ... I seriously doubt that there are many people now in their late 30s and early 40s who didn't smoke pot."
Benfey said Buckley smoked marijuana regularly, "like everybody else," while a student at Hampshire.
